side.notes: Exact licensed live-fish pages and the comparative diagnosis constrain the miniature elongate Cory outline, short rounded snout, inferior mouth, conspicuous continuous stripe, translucent fins and forked caudal.

top.uncertainty: Moderate to high. An oblique exact-species image constrains the taper qualitatively, but no verified whole-body orthographic dorsal original was found.
top.notes: Half-width stations preserve a narrow trunk, broader armored cheek region and narrow peduncle. They are not claimed as calibrated soft-tissue measurements.

front.uncertainty: Moderate to high. Oblique live-fish views reveal relative head breadth and barbel placement, but no verified orthographic frontal original was found.
front.notes: The small inferior lips, paired barbels, seated eyes and flattened belly are conservative Corydoradinae interpretations bounded by exact-species oblique views.

silhouetteLandmarks.name: miniature elongate armored trunk rather than a stocky common-Cory capsule
silhouetteLandmarks.notes: The station sequence keeps the two-centimeter body lower and more elongate than Bronze Cory while retaining a gently arched armored back and relatively flat ventral surface.

silhouetteLandmarks.name: short rounded snout, small inferior mouth and tapered barbels
silhouetteLandmarks.notes: The revised head stations taper sooner and more narrowly into the rounded snout. A much smaller mouth radius and width, lower jaw placement, shallow separated lip arcs and shorter finer barbels replace the rejected candidate's large terminal sucker ring.

silhouetteLandmarks.name: narrow peduncle with a moderately forked translucent caudal
silhouetteLandmarks.notes: Early posterior taper leads into a small peduncle and forked tail. The fin remains lightly ray-marked and translucent rather than opaque or paddle-shaped.

silhouetteLandmarks.name: two lateral armor rows with delicate leading fin spines
silhouetteLandmarks.notes: Two narrower, separated procedural plate rows now receive stronger normal relief and bounded color contrast. They preserve armored-catfish identity without importing the oversized scutes or spines of the much larger Bronze Cory.

proportions.name: maximum adult standard length
proportions.notes: FishBase reports 2.1 cm standard length. The source uses that value as the conservative visible display reference and records the scope rather than inventing a total-length conversion.

proportions.name: maximum body depth divided by station-defined standard length
proportions.uncertainty: Moderate. The exact lateral photographs constrain a visibly slender outline but do not include a calibration ruler or verified orthographic setup.
proportions.notes: The deepest station is approximately 30.8 percent of the 17.2 mm station-defined snout-to-caudal-base length, preserving the exact images' slender dwarf profile.

proportions.name: maximum body width relative to maximum body depth
proportions.uncertainty: Moderate to high. The exact image is oblique and supplies no scale, so the ratio is a conservative soft-tissue estimate rather than a measured orthographic value.
proportions.notes: The maximum full width remains smaller than vertical depth while the armored cheek region stays broader than the caudal peduncle.

proportions.name: caudal length relative to visible display reference
proportions.uncertainty: Moderate. Aquarium photographs constrain a modest forked caudal but do not provide a calibrated standard-to-total-length ratio.
proportions.notes: The caudal is large enough to read as forked and mobile without overwhelming the tiny armored body.

colorPatternBoundaries.name: thick continuous dark mid-lateral stripe from snout to peduncle
colorPatternBoundaries.notes: The revised mask is narrower across the flank, rises through the exact eye station and snout region, then tapers at the peduncle. It replaces the rejected candidate's broad low stripe without becoming a tail spot, broken dash or whole-side dark wash.

colorPatternBoundaries.name: pearl-grey flank, darker back and pale lower surface
colorPatternBoundaries.notes: The procedural ground separates a subdued grey dorsal field from a lighter belly and retains low-contrast iridescence without turning bronze, gold or uniform beige.

colorPatternBoundaries.name: hyaline adipose and translucent ray-marked fins
colorPatternBoundaries.notes: Fin alpha, ray contrast and normal strength are reduced throughout, with an additional adipose alpha reduction. This replaces the rejected opaque beige sheets with hyaline membranes and restrained leading-spine cues.

reviewedCandidate.notes: Independent visual review found the repaired dwarf silhouette, inferior mouth, raised tapered stripe, armor-row treatment, hyaline fins and forked tail suitable for explicit user review. This receipt is not user acceptance and does not authorize promotion.

mismatches.note: The preserved candidate has a bulbous blunt head, conspicuous terminal sucker ring and overlong whisker read. Revised head stations, an inferior jaw offset, smaller transverse lip arcs and shorter finer barbels address those source-level failures.
The preserved candidate's stripe is too broad and low, missing the eye region. The revised mask narrows the band, raises it through the eye and snout, and tapers it into the caudal peduncle.

The preserved candidate reads as smooth because both armor rows are visually lost. The revised backend separates the row centers and increases bounded normal and color relief while keeping the plates shallow.

The preserved dorsal, adipose, anal, caudal and paired fins read as opaque beige sheets. Lower alpha, reduced ray contrast, reduced fin-normal strength and an extra hyaline adipose treatment address the mismatch.
Whole-body width and frontal trunk depth remain explicitly inferred. The reviewed fable-v2 candidate must not be represented as measured and should retain a conservative narrow body.
The smaller inferior transverse mouth is materially improved, but the frontal view may still make the lip edges read slightly more prominent than the subtle live-fish reference.
Both armor rows now read under the reviewed lighting, although their shallow relief remains intentionally subtle and may soften further at game scale.
Independent review covered the recorded candidate surfaces. Barbel, fin and body deformation through the complete animation range remains a downstream runtime caveat.

failedCandidateEvidence.review: Independent visual review rejected the large terminal sucker ring, low broad stripe, hidden armor rows, bulbous head and opaque beige fins. The correct dwarf silhouette and forked tail remain preserved as the repair baseline.
